summary: This standards-track document describes the use of the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm in the Internet Key Exchange Protocol version 2.

eli5.summary: Computers building a secure tunnel can prove who they are with a modern signature method. This says how.

questions: how to use eddsa in ikev2
what is the identity hash in ikev2
subtitle: How IKEv2 peers signal and use EdDSA signatures, which need no separate hashing step.

tldr.problem: IKEv2 signature negotiation assumes every signature scheme hashes a message first, but EdDSA accepts messages of arbitrary size and needs no prehashing.
tldr.mechanism: A new "Identity" (5) value in the IKEv2 Hash Algorithms registry is placed in the SIGNATURE_HASH_ALGORITHMS notification to say no hashing is performed.
tldr.outcome: Peers can use Ed25519 and Ed448 in IKEv2. The prehashed variants Ed25519ph and Ed448ph MUST NOT be used.

today: RFC 8420 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Signatures Without Prehashing
sections.content:
IKEv2 can use arbitrary signature algorithms (RFC 7427). Each side lists its supported hash algorithms in the SIGNATURE_HASH_ALGORITHMS notification, which assumes every scheme hashes first and then signs.

EdDSA (RFC 8032) does not need that. Its methods, Ed25519 and Ed448, use the Edwards 25519 and Edwards 448 curves and accept messages of any size. Prehashed versions exist, but are not recommended where buffering the whole message is easy, which is true of IKEv2.
sections.eli5: Most signing methods first squash a message into a small summary. This newer method can sign the whole message directly.

sections.title: The Identity Hash Identifier
sections.content:
The document defines a value called Identity (5) in the IKEv2 Hash Algorithms registry. Including it in the notification means the receiver supports at least one signature algorithm that takes arbitrary-size messages, such as Ed25519 and Ed448.

Ed25519 and Ed448 are only defined with the Identity hash and MUST NOT be sent to a receiver that has not indicated support for it. The prehashed Ed25519ph and Ed448ph MUST NOT be used in IKE.
sections.eli5: A peer says "I can sign without squashing first" by sending a special label. Nobody sends this kind of signature unless the other side said it understands.

sections.title: Security and Registry Notes
sections.content:
Identity is needed only for algorithms that accept arbitrary-size input, and it MUST NOT be used if none of the supported and configured algorithms do. There is no good reason to prehash inputs for such algorithms, so implementations MUST include Identity in the notification when EdDSA is supported and configured, and SHOULD NOT list other hash algorithms if all configured signature algorithms have this property.

IANA assigned value 5 for Identity. An appendix repeats the object identifiers from RFC 8410: id-Ed25519 is 1.3.101.112 and id-Ed448 is 1.3.101.113, both with absent parameters.
sections.eli5: Use the special label only when you really have this kind of signing, and then do not bother offering the older squash-first methods.
